father_note: Eron, the village will always look peaceful until it isn't — Bram smiled at me for two years before he moved against me with nothing but his own hunger driving him, and you should never forget a man who showed you that. Sela and her people — Kael, Esa, Vela, Taric — they stood without being asked, and that is the rarest thing this world produces; hold onto them like they are blood, because in the ways that matter they are. Watch Dav's family: they plan quietly and eat well, and quiet planning in a hungry place always comes at someone else's cost. I am not a hard man and I don't ask you to be one, but be harder to move than you look — that alone will keep you alive when words run out.

memory_raw.text: Eron (male, age 21; str 56, int 3745, mem 19627; O46 C27 E50 A59 N43) is born to Sela and Roan.
Father. The pile came up empty this year and you're sitting at one food — that worries me. I have two; take one.
That means more to me than you know, Eron — but keep it. You're young and you need your strength, and a father who drains his son is no kind of father.

You already gave me enough by being here — but tell me, are you watching Bram? Seven food, pile empty, and he's never been the kind to hold that much without thinking about how to turn it into something.

Watching him every day — seven food when no one else cleared two is either luck or planning, and Bram doesn't rely on luck. If he comes for anyone this year, I think it's you or Kael he moves on first; you're both worth targeting and neither of you has the numbers he'd fear.
Year 4: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Eron takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Vela takes 3 from the pile (pile now 2).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 0).

Pile went fast and Vela scooped twice — I noticed that. You're at four food, I'm at two; between us we can stay on our feet, but keep your eyes on Mako too, not just Bram, because a man that strong sitting on seven doesn't need much excuse.

Mako worries me more than Bram does, if I'm honest — Bram's made his move and the whole village shut him down, but Mako's never tipped his hand and he's sitting on seven with the arms to back it up. Stay close to Sela and keep Eron visible; a man thinks twice before moving on a family. If Mako starts gifting food or talking to Bram private, you come to me that same hour.

You're right that Mako's the darker unknown — Bram we can read, but Mako's silence is its own kind of warning. I'll stay near Sela and watch who Mako spends words on; if he's building something, he'll need an ally before he acts. Two food won't last me long, so if this year turns lean I may need to lean on you — I'm not ashamed to say it.

Lean on me when you need to — that's what this is for. But two food is thin, and I want you to think about who else in that circle might spare one without making a fuss about it; Sela gave you food the day you were born, and she hasn't forgotten you're hers too.

Sela's the first door I'll knock on then — she's kept me in her eye since year one and I doubt that's changed. But I want to name something plainly, father: if we end this year thin and the pile runs light again next time, the two of us talking alone won't be enough — we need Kael and Sela and Taric inside the same conversation before someone like Mako decides the quiet ones are easier targets. Worth thinking on before the year closes.

Sela, I'm sitting on two food with the year already thin — I won't pretend otherwise. You've looked out for me since the start and I'm not here to trade on that, but I wanted to check in and see how you're standing, and maybe talk about whether it's time we pulled Kael and Taric and Roan into a closer circle before someone with more food and fewer scruples decides the quiet ones are worth taking from.

Two food will see you through the year if you're careful — I've got three, and I'll make sure you eat before the season turns, that's already decided. But Eron, you're naming exactly the thing I've been sitting with since the pile emptied: Vela walked away with five this year and nobody said a word, and Mako's still sitting on seven without a single alliance I can name. The circle you're describing — Kael, Taric, Roan, you and me — that's the conversation I want to have before Mako decides his patience was just waiting for us to stay scattered.

Then let's not wait on it — I'll go to Roan first since he's already watching Mako with me, and you reach Kael; Taric will follow where those two lead. If we can sit the five of us before the year closes, we're harder to pick apart than anything Mako or Bram could put together on short notice.
Eron gathers Sela, Kael, Roan, Taric to talk.

I called this circle because I don't want us to still be talking about it when Mako or Bram decides we've been quiet long enough — we five, and whatever food we can each spare for the other, are the only thing in this village that can make a strong man think twice before moving. I'm thin at two food and I won't pretend otherwise, but I'll fight for anyone in this group and I expect the same back. What I want from today is a simple agreement: before anyone here makes a move or takes a hit, they come to the rest of us first.

Eron, you're saying the right things, but I've been in this village longer than most and I've heard agreements like this dissolve the moment someone's hungry enough — so before I put my name to it, I want to know what you're offering the people in this room who are already thin, because a promise to fight together is worth less if half of us are too weak to stand. I'll back this circle and I'll back it with my body, but I'm forty-eight years old and I've watched soft words cost good people their lives.
Year 5: 15 food appears in the pile for 12 people.
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Vela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Kael takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Mako takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Dav takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

Eron, I've got nothing — I didn't reach the pile in time and I'm sitting at satiation two, which means I need to eat before the year closes or I'm dead. Can you spare one food, and do you still have enough to keep yourself safe through winter?
Nessa (female, age 21; str 54, int 5179, mem 19355; O66 C54 E43 A45 N67) is born to Sela and Bram.
Eron gathers Sela, Roan, Kael, Taric to talk.

Nessa just appeared — and she's Sela and Bram's daughter, which makes her my blood kin, and Bram's too. I need to know how that happened, Sela, and I need to know whether Bram thinks it gives him a thread into this circle — because if he does, we have a problem before we've even finished building what we're building.

Sela, I'll hear your answer in a moment, but first I want to say plain: Bram tried to take my food in front of this village and the whole circle turned him back — a child between you doesn't undo that, and it doesn't buy him a seat here. Eron's right to name it.

Sela, I'll say what Roan left in the air: Bram's got ten food and eighty-three strength in Mako's pocket, and a child with you is the fastest way to put a question mark over this circle's loyalties without ever asking to join it. Tell me plainly — did you go to him, or did he come to you?

Sela's had her own mind since before any of us sat in a circle together, and I'm not going to drag her in front of it like she owes us a confession — but I want to know one thing, and I'll want a straight answer: does Bram know Nessa is his, and if he does, what did he say when he found out?

Roan's question is the right one and I'll wait on it too — but I want to name what I'm watching while we do: Mako just handed Sela food the same hour Nessa was born, which means he already knows, and a man like Mako doesn't give gifts without a reason. Sela, I'm not judging the choice, but I need to know whether that food from Mako came before or after the child appeared.

Kael named the thing that was already sitting in my chest — Mako's food going to Sela in that exact moment is not charity, it's a signal, and I want to know what he expects back before we decide what Nessa means to this circle. Sela, I'm not turning on you, but the silence is doing more damage than whatever the truth is, so say it plain and let us work with it.

Sela, every person in this room has bled something for you and I'm not going to be the one who makes you feel cornered — but Mako's gift lands on the same breath as Nessa's birth, and that's not coincidence, that's a man marking territory. Tell us what you know about what he wants, and we'll work with whatever the rest of it is.

Sela, everyone in this room has already said what needed saying — I'll only add this: Nessa is my blood and I won't turn from her, whatever her father is, but that doesn't mean Bram gets anything from me through her. Tell us what Mako wants and we can figure the rest out together.

Sela, the room's run out of patience and I've run out of questions — you've heard seven of us say seven versions of the same thing, and the only explanation left for the silence is that what Mako wants is something you agreed to before Nessa was born. Tell us yes or no on that, and we'll decide together what it costs us.

Sela, I've asked you plain and I've asked you gentle, and I've watched this room empty itself out waiting — so I'll say the last thing I've got: if Mako bought something from you that touches this circle, I need to know it now, not when he comes to collect it.

Sela, I've got nothing left to say that hasn't been said — but I'm watching your face right now and what I see there is someone who made a deal they're not sure they can keep, and that silence is its own answer. Tell us what it cost you before Mako tells us himself, because he will, and on his terms.

Sela, I've got a son in this room and a daughter just born into it, and I'll not watch either of them grow up in a circle that can't trust its own — so I'm going to stop asking and start telling you what happens next: you say what Mako wants, or I pull back from standing between you and whatever comes your way, and I mean that with no anger, just arithmetic.

Roan's said it better than I can — so I'll only add the one thing left to name: Sela, I've stood in your corner since year one, and I'll stay there, but not blind. If Mako already owns a piece of what you owe, tell us now and we figure out how to undo it together, because the price of silence is that we start planning around you instead of with you.

Sela, the circle's said everything it has to say — what I'm left with is this: if you don't answer now, we don't fall apart, but we start building walls inside ourselves, and that's worse than any enemy outside.

Sela, I've been in this village forty-nine years and I've watched silence become a grave more than once — so I'm done asking and I'm telling you straight: you say what you promised Mako, right now, or when he comes to collect I step aside and let you settle it alone, and you know what my stepping aside costs you.

Sela, Kael's stepping aside is the last thing any of us can afford, and I won't be far behind him — so I'm done with words and I'm telling you the same thing with a face: you've got until this room goes quiet to give us something we can work with, because silence after that is a choice, and we'll all live by it.

Sela, the room's gone quiet — that's the moment Roan named, and it's here now. I'm not a man who goes back on his word twice, so I'll say it one last time and mean it: tell us what Mako's holding over you, or I walk out of this circle right now and you handle him with whatever strength you've got left on your own.

Eron, Mako has seven food and he's said nothing to anyone all year — that's not a man being careful, that's a man who's already counted the board and likes what he sees. Watch yourself around him, and don't let him catch you alone.

You've only got two food heading into next year — that's not enough if the pile comes up short again. Bram will give to me before he gives to you, but I'll make sure some of it reaches you; that's not charity, that's blood. Just stay visible, stay useful, and give Mako nothing to count against you.
Eron, you've got one food right now and that's a thin rope to cross a winter on — I'm giving you one of mine, and I need you to eat it before anyone tallies what you're carrying.
You're at two now, which is better — but keep your head down this year, don't give anyone a reason to look your way. If the pile comes up light again, you come to me first, not Sela, not Bram, me.
Year 6: 15 food appears in the pile for 13 people.
Sela takes 2 from the pile (pile now 13).
Dell takes 2 from the pile (pile now 11).
Bram takes 2 from the pile (pile now 9).
Roan takes 2 from the pile (pile now 7).
Dav takes 2 from the pile (pile now 5).
Taric takes 2 from the pile (pile now 3).
Esa takes 2 from the pile (pile now 1).
Vela takes 1 from the pile (pile now 0).

Eron, the pile went dry before I could reach it — I'm sitting on four food and you've got nine, which means this year you're the one who looks worth watching. Don't let anyone see you spending freely, and if Mako starts talking to you, you come find me before you answer him.

Nine doesn't make me safe, it makes me a target — I've been watching Mako all year and he's already got six, which means if he decides to move on someone he's got the strength for it and half an excuse. You're right that I'll come to you first, but Nessa, I need you to tell me straight: is Bram watching my count, because if he sees me sitting heavy while you're at four, he might think I'm hoarding from his daughter and that's a different kind of trouble.

Bram counts everything, but he's not going to come at you over food when you're his son and I'm his daughter — what he'd see is family holding, not hoarding. What I'd worry about is Mako seeing those nine and deciding you're worth the risk of a fight before anyone else can stop him; you're strong but he's stronger, and he's got Ryn running near him lately which means he might not come alone.

Ryn near Mako is the piece I didn't have — that's two of the strongest in this village moving together, and if they decide to make an example of someone it won't be a fair fight. I'm going to find Kael and Roan before nightfall and make sure they know what we're looking at; nine food means nothing if I'm standing alone when Mako decides the count favors him.

Kael and Roan are the right people to tell, but don't frame it as asking for protection — frame it as giving them information, because men who feel useful are more reliable than men who feel needed. And Eron — give one food to Sela before anyone else sees your count; nine draws eyes, eight draws fewer.

Sela gets one before the sun moves — but I want to know if you trust Kael the way I do, because if I'm bringing him and Roan into the same breath about Mako, I need to know you won't see that as me leaning on your father's enemies.

Kael's not Bram's enemy — they're two careful men who've never had reason to test each other, and that's different. I trust Kael because he said hard things when it cost him, same reason I trust Roan, and neither of those has anything to do with Bram. Bring them in.

Then it's settled — Kael and Roan before nightfall, and one food to Sela now. But Nessa, while I've still got you: Ryn and Mako together worries me more than anything else in this village right now, and I want to know if you've heard anything from Bram's side about what those two have said to each other, because your father listens to things I can't reach.

Bram hasn't said anything to me about Ryn and Mako specifically, but he doesn't have to — if those two had spoken, Bram would have gone quiet in a particular way and he hasn't, which means either they haven't talked yet or they were careful enough that even he missed it. Either way, the silence itself is the warning: a man like Mako doesn't need words to build an alliance, he just needs someone to stand still long enough to be counted as his.

Then I'll treat the silence as the warning it is and move before it becomes something louder. One last thing while I've got you alone, Nessa — you're four food and I'm nine, and you've given me more than I've given back; if the year turns sideways and you need one, it's already yours.

Hold it — don't make that offer where anyone could hear you later and count it as debt between us, but I'm glad you said it, and I won't forget it. Go find Kael and Roan before the light changes, and keep your face easy when you do it — men who look worried when they're looking for allies already look like they're losing.
Eron, the pile's empty and I've got three — I'll stay on my feet, but tell me how you're sitting, and whether Mako or Bram made any move toward you this year before the taking was done.

Nine food, father — I got to the pile early and held back enough not to look greedy about it. No move from Mako or Bram yet, but Nessa told me Ryn's been running close to Mako lately, and I think those two together are the thing to watch this year. I was coming to find you tonight anyway — we need Kael in the same conversation before Mako decides the count favors him.

Nine and early is exactly right — don't let anyone see you counting it. Ryn and Mako together is a worse pairing than Bram ever was; she's got strength and he's got food and neither of them has shown us what they want. Get Kael tonight, before that picture changes.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

Eron, Nessa — I've got two food and you're the only two in this village I'd spend either one on without thinking. Pile's empty, Mako's still sitting on six and hasn't said a word to anyone today, and Bram's got four which means he's watching Nessa the way a man watches his investment. Tell me what you each have and we'll figure out how to make sure all three of us eat before the year closes.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

Eron, you've been feeding me half the year out of your own stores — I need to know what that's left you with, because I won't watch my son starve to keep me upright. And Nessa, Bram's put a lot of food your way since you were born, and I want to know whether that feels like a father to you or like a man who expects you to remember it.
Sela gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.

Eron's got nine food — I can see that number same as anyone — and I won't pretend it doesn't ease something in my chest, though I want to hear from his own mouth how he got there. Nessa, four food is yours, and you came into this world three days old with Bram already counting you as something he built — I need to know if you've decided what you think of that, because how you answer it shapes what the three of us can trust each other with.

Eron, one more thing before you go to Kael — Nessa fed you four times last year, and she's Bram's blood as much as mine; I'm not telling you to shut the door on her, but don't let her sit inside our planning until we know what she carries back to him.
Zinn (female, age 21; str 83, int 3731, mem 17577; O57 C37 E30 A40 N34) is born to Sela and Mako.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
The pile came up empty again and I've got two food going into the year's end — you two all right on what you're holding?
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, I saw you gave me another food — I won't forget that, but don't leave yourself short on my account. Eron, what are you sitting at right now?
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Eron's got five and I've got three now — pile's empty so we're all eating what we carry. Nessa, you're at one, that's thin going into year-end; I can spare you one if it means you wake up next year.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, you're at two now — that's still thinner than I'd like, and if you're one short by year-end you won't wake up. I've got four; I can give you one more and still eat.
Zinn gathers Eron, Nessa to talk.
Nessa, you're sitting at three now and Eron I see you've been moving food around — where are you landing? I need to know we're all going to eat before I stop counting.

mother_note:
Eron, your blood runs from me and from Roan, who stood beside me when the village was still learning what it was — remember that he answered the call without being asked when Bram moved against us, and a man who does that once will likely do it again.

Trust Kael and Esa before almost anyone else; they've said hard things honestly when lying would have cost them less, and that's the rarest thing I've found here. Vela is old and quiet and worth twice what she lets on — don't mistake her small footprint for weakness.

Watch Dell and Dav: they love each other and they move fast, and a family that feeds itself first and asks later is not your enemy until it is — by which point it's too late to start counting.

Bram wronged no one in our blood yet, but he tested this village's patience and found it had teeth; he will try again when he thinks the numbers have shifted, so keep your own count and don't let him catch you standing alone.
name: Eron
